source.title: Generalization bounds via distillation
source.authors: Daniel J. Hsu; Zi-Wei Ji; Matus Telgarsky; Lan Wang

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies distillation and generalization bounds, but its experiments do not test any listed claim version. Its measurements concern bounds and margin distributions rather than the specified behaviors or gap-tracking property.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test errors and generalization-bound changes during distillation, width-dependent margin histograms, and margin changes under label randomization. These findings do not test the listed versions: the paper does not report random-label test accuracy, test error across widths past interpolation, architecture comparisons, optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout effects, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples.
record.test_reason: Figure 3 reports similar MNIST test errors for widths 64, 256 and 1024, all trained to zero training error. This bears on V2 in a deeper network setting, although the qualitative description cannot establish whether test error keeps decreasing.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate. The main theoretical contribution transfers bounds from a distilled network to the original network under assumptions on data augmentation. Experiments show substantially smaller bounds with similar predictions and low test error; the stable-rank bound still fails to achieve full width independence.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments train networks and then distill them to study bounds, errors, and margin distributions; they do not apply the interventions in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that outcomes vary with network width, distillation stage, and the fraction of labels permuted.

fits_no_version.finding: Progressive distillation reduces bounds by roughly ten orders of magnitude while training and test errors initially change little.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distillation can substantially improve calculated generalization bounds while preserving predictive performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalized margin histograms differ across widths before distillation and become nearly identical afterward.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distillation can reduce the width dependence of these normalized margin distributions.

fits_no_version.finding: Randomizing even 25% of labels substantially shrinks normalized margins after distillation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distilled normalized margins respond strongly to label randomization.

record.problems: The reported experimental results are largely presented as figures; exact per-condition values and uncertainty estimates are not stated in the text. Several reported findings concern bounds or margin histograms rather than test error or training-test gaps.

untested.parts: Near-perfect random-label fit together with natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Whether test error continues decreasing beyond interpolation; the interpolation threshold, one-hidden-layer recipe and CIFAR-10 setting are not evaluated.
Held-out comparisons between convolutional and fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity.
Comparative optimizer generalization under controlled tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps and comparisons against other measures.
Removing memorized examples versus equally sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: No V2 verdict is justified: similar test errors can conceal small decreases or increases. Rows linked to none receive cannot_determine relative to the listed claims, although their reported distillation or margin effects are observed.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels are not compared.
Test error is not swept across widths beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional and fully connected networks are not compared for test error.
Adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers are not compared for held-out performance.
Batch size and its effects on held-out performance are not varied.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its relationship to the training-test gap are not measured.
Memorized examples are not identified, removed, or compared with random removals.

rows.subject: ResNet8
rows.operation_detail: Progressive distillation trades off complexity against distillation distance.

conditions.value: generalization bounds, training error, testing error

rows.measure: Generalization bound and generalization measure during distillation; training and testing errors.
rows.baseline: Initial network; exact values for each curve are figure only.
rows.value: The bounds drop by nearly 10^10 in the initial phase while training and testing errors hardly change; initial test error 0.067.
rows.note: The paper reports the curve values only in the figure; the text describes the trend and gives the initial test error.
rows.check: The distillation result is accurately summarized but measures none of V1–V8. The observed reduction concerns bounds, not magnitude-aware sharpness.

rows.subject: 6-layer fully connected networks, widths 64, 256, and 1024
rows.stage_stated: trained until training error zero; then distilled
rows.operation_detail: Compared normalized margin histograms across widths before and after distillation.
rows.measure: Normalized margin distributions; test errors are described as similar.
rows.value: Before distillation, margin distributions differ across widths; test errors are described as similar.
rows.note: No per-width test-error values are reported; the result concerns margin histograms, not a test-error sweep.
rows.check: The reported similar test errors across widths, each attaining zero training error, bear on V2. However, similarity alone cannot establish a decreasing, flat or increasing trend; no per-width errors are supplied. These are six-layer networks rather than the original one-hidden-layer setting.

rows.subject: 6-layer fully connected networks, widths 64, 256, and 1024
rows.operation_detail: Compared normalized margin histograms across widths after distillation.
rows.value: After distillation, margin histograms are nearly identical.
rows.note: This is a finding about normalized margin histograms, not a measurement of the gap-tracking property in V7.
rows.check: Nearly identical normalized margin histograms after distillation do not establish decreasing test error with width or the sharpness relationship in V7.

rows.subject: 6-layer fully connected network, width 256
rows.stage_stated: trained with vanilla SGD; then distilled
rows.operation_detail: Permuted different fractions of labels and compared margin histograms.
rows.baseline: 0% labels permuted; figure reports distillation distance approximately 0.003.
rows.value: The margin distribution collapses to zero across the reported label-permutation conditions; even randomizing 25% shrinks it significantly.
rows.note: The paper does not report random-label training accuracy, held-out accuracy, or test error for these conditions.
rows.check: The normalized-margin result does not report random-label training fit or held-out performance required by V1. The caption's collapse description should not imply that the 0% control has the same distribution as randomized conditions: the discussion explicitly reports substantial shrinkage upon randomizing 25%.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
